name: Browse AI
tagline: No-code web robots for monitoring, extraction, and scheduled data delivery

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited robots; 2 websites; 3 users; 90-day data retention; monitoring no more frequent than hourly
tiers.notes: The live first-party page did not expose a stable numeric monthly-credit allowance for Free.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.limits: 2,000 credits on monthly billing or 12,000 credits/year paid upfront; 5 websites; 3 users; unlimited robots; 90-day retention; 5-minute monitoring
tiers.notes: The annual allowance averages 1,000 credits/month but is issued for the annual term.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 5,000 credits/month or 60,000 credits/year; 10 websites; 10 users; unlimited robots; 90-day retention; 5-minute monitoring

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Custom credits, websites and users; managed onboarding and higher-scale automation
tiers.notes: Starts at $6,000/year and is billed annually.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited robots, 2 websites, 3 users, 90-day retention and hourly monitoring; numeric monthly credits were not reliably exposed on the current page
pricing.billingTerms: free + monthly or annual Personal/Professional; Premium is annual-only from $6,000/year; credits reset by billing period and do not carry over
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra websites cost $5/month on monthly Personal or $4/month annual, and $3/month monthly or $2.40/month annual on Professional; some premium-site runs consume 2-10+ credits; 1 credit covers only 10 extracted rows or 1 screenshot, and unused credits expire

verdictSummary: The visible web data extraction loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Browse AI earns its keep through connectors, auth, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build one explicit web data extraction workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: API credentials for the two chosen services
whatYouLose: schema drift handling and enterprise controls
whyPeopleStillPay: Browse AI: One automation is easy. Subscribers pay for maintained integrations, credentials, retries, observability, and someone else owning breakage.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, rate limits, webhooks, retries, queues, idempotency, logs, secret rotation, and third-party API changes.

priorArt.name: Activepieces
priorArt.desc: Open-source automation builder with connectors and self-hosting.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Browse AI is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Browse AI, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build one explicit web data extraction workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: OAuth app verification; durable execution at scale; schema drift handling and enterprise controls.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
